work.title: INTERVIEW SYNTHESIS
work.subtitle: 访谈综合报告
work.scope: Entirely synthetic report exercise: source records, statements and version events are invented. Illustrations are not empirical evidence. No actual study, operational result, market research or participant interview is supplied.

pages.title: Synthesize invented extracts transparently.
pages.lead: This report demonstrates qualitative synthesis using six authored example extracts. No interviews were conducted, and the text contains no actual participants, consent records or personal data.
pages.body: The extracts concern finding and interpreting a fictional prompt card. Nine tag assignments cover four themes because an extract can receive more than one tag. Six extracts and nine tags must not be presented as nine people or as a representative study.
pages.detail: Separate the supplied synthetic result from your interpretation and any real-world evidence still needed.
pages.question: What should a reader know before interpreting any theme in this report?

pages.title: Describe the inquiry guide.
pages.lead: A guide states what a real conversation might explore without implying that those questions have already been asked. Here the guide is a proposed scaffold for interpreting the invented examples.
pages.body: Possible questions concern locating a current card, recognising a revision and asking for clarification. A genuine interview study would require appropriate context, recruitment, consent and review. None of those activities is supplied by the example text.

pages.title: Keep the material unit honest.
pages.lead: E1–E6 identify six invented extracts, not six interviewees. The source intentionally contains no demographic attributes or participant identifiers.
pages.body: A real synthesis would explain how material was produced and selected. Here the full set is authored for the template, so it can illustrate coding mechanics but cannot support claims about prevalence, saturation, needs or experiences of actual people.

pages.title: Make coding choices visible.
pages.lead: A code links a passage to an analytic label. It is a decision by the analyst, not a fact automatically contained in the words. The exported source records every stipulated tag.
pages.body: The codebook uses findability, clarification, version and example. E1 receives findability and version; E2 receives findability and clarification. Multiple coding explains why theme assignments outnumber extracts. No independent coder agreement is supplied.

pages.title: Cluster without ranking needs.
pages.lead: Findability appears in E1, E2 and E6; clarification in E2, E3 and E5; version in E1 and E4; example in E3. The counts are 3, 3, 2 and 1.
pages.body: Those nine assignments describe this authored coding table only. They do not rank real user needs or estimate how common a view is. Preserve the source identifiers with each theme rather than treating the largest count as a validated priority.

pages.title: Keep contrasting situations visible.
pages.lead: An extract about identifying a version differs from one about asking another person for clarification. Both may concern interpretation, but collapsing them can hide the different situations described.
pages.body: E4 refers to keeping an earlier version for comparison. E5 asks whom to approach about an unfamiliar term. The contrast suggests questions about change visibility and help routes, not findings about actual behaviours or preferences.

pages.title: Record the analyst’s influence.
pages.lead: A reflexive note identifies how the question and codebook shape the synthesis. In this teaching set, the same author created the extracts and the tags, so the grouping cannot be treated as independent evidence.
pages.body: The decision to use findability as a code makes certain phrases more visible. A different question could lead to a different grouping. State that influence directly rather than presenting the theme map as the only possible reading.

pages.title: State the finding boundary.
pages.lead: A useful exercise synthesis describes an interpretation of the examples and the question it raises. It should not claim actual research insights, validated needs or a tested service improvement.
pages.body: A bounded statement is that the six invented extracts illustrate several ways to discuss card interpretation: finding, clarifying, recognising versions and using examples. The statement remains about the teaching material, not about real readers.
